title: Best GE Dehumidifier (2026): APYR50LC and Every Model Compared
h1: The Best GE Dehumidifiers, From the APYR50LC Down
dek: GE's lineup is short and sensible: two pump-equipped 50-pints, a 35 and a 20. Here's which one fits your space — and how to fix the most common hiccups.
description: The best GE dehumidifiers for 2026, led by the GE APYR50LC with pump. Compare 20, 35 and 50-pint models, plus GE filter, manual and P1 code help.
intro: If you want one GE dehumidifier and no more spec-sheet homework, the **GE APYR50LC** is it: 50 pints a day, a built-in pump that lifts water up to 16 feet, and coverage for roughly 4,500 sq ft of basement or garage. It has earned best-overall nods from independent reviewers, and it's the model most GE shoppers end up searching for by name.

GE doesn't build its dehumidifiers itself. Like several big appliance brands, it sources them from Midea, which means GE units share a lot of DNA with Midea's own machines and some Frigidaire models. What sets GE apart is its model tiers, its SmartHQ app on the connected version, and wide availability at big-box stores.
We compared GE's current range using spec sheets, manuals, ENERGY STAR data and owner reviews, and added a quick troubleshooting guide for the filter, manual and error-code questions owners ask most.
topPicksLead: The **GE APYR50LC** is the best GE dehumidifier for most basements, pairing full 50-pint capacity with a pump that gets water up and out without a floor drain.

products.name: GE 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Built-In Pump (APYR50LC)
pros: Built-in pump lifts water up to 16 feet
Gravity drain spout as a backup option
Rated for up to about 4,500 sq ft
1.7-gallon tank buffers runtime if the pump line is off
cons: No app control on this version
products.whyWeLoveIt: Most basements don't have a floor drain where you need one. The APYR50LC solves that with a pump that pushes water up to a sink or out a window, so you can set a target humidity and walk away for the season.
products.performance: GE rates it at 50 pints a day and up to roughly 4,500 sq ft, which covers a full basement, garage or utility area. The 16-foot pump lift is generous enough to reach a laundry sink or a basement window well. Independent reviewers have ranked it among the best overall dehumidifiers of 2026, and owners consistently cite the pump as the reason they'd buy it again. If you'd rather compare it with other self-draining units, see our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.
products.notes: Keep the pump hose free of kinks and below the unit's maximum lift; a pinched or overlong line is the usual cause of pump errors.

products.name: GE 50-Pint Smart Dehumidifier with Pump (ADHR50LZ)
pros: SmartHQ app with full-tank and filter alerts
Alexa and Google Assistant voice control
Smart Dry mode adjusts fan speed automatically
Same pump and capacity as the APYR50LC
cons: Costs more for the same drying hardware
App features are only useful if you'll use them
products.whyWeLoveIt: If the dehumidifier lives in a finished basement you rarely visit, a phone alert before something goes wrong is genuinely valuable. The ADHR50LZ adds that SmartHQ layer to the same pump-equipped 50-pint machine.
products.performance: Underneath, it matches the APYR50LC: 50 pints a day, about 4,500 sq ft of coverage and a built-in pump. On top, SmartHQ tracks energy use, sends empty-bucket and filter-cleaning reminders, and lets you change the setpoint by voice. Smart Dry mode nudges the fan speed up or down based on the humidity reading. Browse other connected options in our [best Wi-Fi dehumidifier](/best/best-wifi-dehumidifier/) roundup.

products.name: GE 35-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (ADEL35LZ)
pros: Simple digital controls with three fan speeds
Gravity hose connection for continuous draining
cons: 1.1-gallon tank fills quickly in a wet space
products.whyWeLoveIt: Not every space is a soggy basement. For a bedroom over a slab, a home office or a lightly used lower level that's merely damp, the ADEL35LZ does the job without paying for a pump you won't use.
products.performance: It's rated at 35 pints a day and is ENERGY STAR certified, so it's economical over a long humid season. Drainage is bucket or gravity hose only, which works well if there's a floor drain nearby. Owners describe it as straightforward and reliable for mid-size rooms. Unsure whether 35 pints is enough? Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) breaks it down by room and dampness.

products.name: GE 20-Pint Dehumidifier (ADEL20LY)
pros: Easy to tuck into a closet or utility corner
cons: Sized for about 800 sq ft at most
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a single damp room, a large closet or a small bathroom, the ADEL20LY is the right-sized GE. It costs the least and still includes auto-defrost, which is unusual at this size.
products.performance: It removes 20 pints a day and suits spaces up to roughly 800 sq ft. Run it in anything bigger and it'll run constantly without catching up, so size up to the ADEL35LZ instead. The 6.8-pint tank means frequent emptying in very humid weather, or you can attach a gravity hose. For other compact choices, see our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: Frigidaire 50-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (FHDD5034W1)
pros: Same 50-pint class as GE's top models
Widely stocked, so easy to price-shop
cons: Being replaced by the newer FHDD5034Y1
products.whyWeLoveIt: GE and Frigidaire compete head to head at 50 pints, often with closely related hardware. If the Frigidaire is better priced the week you shop and you have a floor drain, it's an equally sensible buy.
products.performance: It offers 50-pint-class capacity with a set-a-number humidistat and a gravity-drain connection, and it's ENERGY STAR certified for season-long running. The newer FHDD5034Y1 uses R-32 refrigerant and is gradually replacing it at retailers. Compare the full range in our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide.

sections.heading: How we pick the best GE dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't run a test lab. We compare GE's published capacity, coverage and pump specs against ENERGY STAR listings and the owner's manuals, check the CPSC recall database, and weigh results from reputable independent reviewers. Then we read owner reviews at scale to spot recurring failures — pumps that quit, sensors that drift, buckets that leak — and rank each model by who it suits best.

sections.heading: What to look for in a GE dehumidifier

items.label: Read the model prefix
items.text: APYR and ADHR mean pump-equipped 50-pint models; ADEL is the gravity-drain line in 20 and 35 pints. You'll also see related ADEW20LY and ADEW35LZ listings at the same sizes — check the spec sheet to confirm features before buying.

items.label: A pump if there's no low drain
items.text: Only the 50-pint GEs pump. If water has to go up to a sink or out a window, that rules out the ADEL models.

items.label: SmartHQ only if you'll use it
items.text: The ADHR50LZ costs more than the APYR50LC for the same drying hardware plus app alerts and voice control.

items.label: The right size
items.text: About 800 sq ft for the 20-pint, a bedroom or small basement for the 35, and a full basement or garage for the 50s.

items.label: Warranty math
items.text: GE's one-year warranty doesn't extend with registration, so compare price per year of coverage against rivals.

sections.heading: GE dehumidifier filter, manual and repair help

blocks.text: Before you call for service or search for parts, check these common fixes. Your GE dehumidifier user manual, available by model number on GE Appliances' website, has the full error table.
What does P1 mean on a GE dehumidifier?

On GE units, **P1** typically signals that the unit is defrosting because the coils got too cold. Leave it running; it clears on its own. If it appears constantly, the room may be too cool for the dehumidifier — see our guide to [dehumidifiers freezing up](/guides/dehumidifier-freezing-up/).

items: Unplug the unit and remove the filter from behind the front grille or above the bucket.
Rinse the mesh in warm water with a little mild detergent; don't use a dishwasher.
Let it dry completely, then slide it back in and reset the filter indicator if your model has one.
**Won't turn on:** check the outlet and that the bucket is seated; a misaligned bucket stops the unit.

**Runs but no water:** the room may already be dry, the filter may be clogged, or the coils may be icing. Our [not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) guide walks through it.
**Hose leaking:** re-seat the hose connection and keep a gravity hose sloping downhill; on pump models, check for kinks.
**Compressor won't start or smells hot:** unplug it and contact GE service rather than ordering parts yourself.

blocks.text: The **GE APYR50LC** is the best GE dehumidifier for most basements and utility rooms: 50 pints a day and a 16-foot pump lift. Step up to the **ADHR50LZ** if SmartHQ alerts and voice control are worth the premium, or down to the **ADEL35LZ** or **ADEL20LY** for smaller spaces that don't need a pump. Because GE's lineup shares a manufacturer with rivals, compare current pricing with Frigidaire before buying, and see our [Haier vs. GE](/compare/haier-vs-ge-dehumidifier/) comparison for another angle.

faqs.q: Is the GE APYR50LC dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: For a basement or garage without a convenient floor drain, yes. It removes 50 pints a day, covers about 4,500 sq ft and has a built-in pump with a 16-foot lift, so you never have to empty a bucket. If you have a drain right next to the unit, a gravity-drain model saves money.
GE's dehumidifiers are built by Midea, which also makes its own Midea-brand units and supplies other appliance brands. GE's SmartHQ app, model tiers and warranty terms are its own.

faqs.q: Where is the filter on a GE dehumidifier?
faqs.a: On most GE models it slides out from behind the front grille or above the water bucket. It's a washable mesh filter: rinse it in warm water every couple of weeks during heavy use, let it dry and reinstall it.

faqs.q: Where can I find my GE dehumidifier manual?
faqs.a: Search your model number, such as APYR50LC or ADEL35LZ, on GE Appliances' website to download the owner's manual and installation instructions. The model number is on a label on the side or back of the unit.

faqs.q: What size GE dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: The 20-pint ADEL20LY suits a single room up to about 800 sq ft, the 35-pint ADEL35LZ handles a bedroom, office or small basement, and the 50-pint APYR50LC or ADHR50LZ covers a full basement or garage up to roughly 4,500 sq ft.

faqs.q: How long is the GE dehumidifier warranty?
faqs.a: GE covers its current dehumidifiers with a one-year limited warranty. Registration doesn't extend it, so keep your receipt and buy from a retailer with a reasonable return window.
